title: Wedding plans with no money
odia:
ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ ନଥାଇ ଧନ
ପୁଅ ବାହା କରି ମନ।
literal_meaning: No money tucked at the waist, yet the mind is set on getting the son married.
meaning_odia: ହାତରେ ସମ୍ବଳ ନଥାଇ ବଡ଼ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ଯୋଜନା କରିବାର ଅସଙ୍ଗତିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପୁଅର ବାହାଘର ଇଚ୍ଛା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ି ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The wish to arrange the son’s wedding runs ahead of the money available. This edition reads the contrast as a reminder to match a plan with the means to carry it out. The saying supplies the pointed wedding image; this practical interpretation is editorial.
usage_example: Someone begins planning a large celebration before working out how to pay for it. These lines could be recalled while discussing a realistic budget. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The money is pictured at the waist, making available funds tangible. A son’s wedding supplies the example of an undertaking that needs resources. The wording specifies no particular ceremony, sum or marriage payment.

witnesses.locator: Saying at inspected page text lines 79–81 and repeated at line 100; both public occurrences have ପୁଅଁ.
witnesses.note: Uploaded PDF page 1, eighth saying, supplies readable ପୁଅ and the two-line arrangement. Its first word contains an empty-box glyph, so only that damaged word is supplied from public ଅଣ୍ଟାରେ. The public witness spells ପୁଅଁ in both occurrences; the display retains uploaded ପୁଅ. This is an explicit composite reading, not an exact transcription of the complete public text or a recovery of the missing uploaded glyph. Shared textual lineage is possible.

origin_note: The uploaded compilation and Hello Odia list contain the saying. Their relationship and earliest source remain unknown; the public list supplies the legible first word used here.

graphic.caption: An imagined wedding plan meets the question of available means.

odia_summary: ସମ୍ବଳ ନଥାଇ ବାହାଘରର ଯୋଜନା—ଇଚ୍ଛା ଓ ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟର ଫରକ।
english_summary: The wish for a wedding runs ahead of the means to arrange it.
